title: Eligibility Category Placement and Precedence
content:
## Placement rule

1. The eligibility category recorded on a Medicaid Managed Care Membership is the one whose entry gate the member meets on the coverage start date.
2. The gate is judged on age in completed years, household income as a percent of the federal poverty level against the category's income floor and income limit, Medicare entitlement, disability determination and, where the category applies an asset test, countable assets.
3. When a member meets more than one category's gate, the category with the lowest placement precedence number is recorded.
4. An income change reported on the state file never moves a member out of a category while that category's continuous eligibility period is running. Outside that period, the new income is applied at the next renewal, not in the middle of an eligibility period.
5. Income is compared as the whole percent printed on the state file, with no rounding by Prairie Ridge.

The figures each clause reads (every category's lowest and highest age, income floor, income limit and placement precedence) are the category's own entry-gate figures.

## Clause by clause

| Clause | Condition | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 and 2 | The member meets exactly one category's entry gate on the coverage start date | That category is recorded |
| 3 | The member meets two or more categories' entry gates | The category with the lowest precedence number is recorded |
| 4 | A new income arrives on the state file while the current category's continuous eligibility period is running | The member stays in the category |
| 4 | A new income arrives outside a continuous eligibility period | The new income is applied at the next renewal |
| 5 | Income on the state file is a whole percent | It is compared as printed; Prairie Ridge does not round it |

## Hypothetical cases

*Hypothetical members and categories, for illustration of the clauses only.*

- A member meets the gates of two categories whose precedence numbers are 3 and 5. The category numbered 3 is recorded.
- A member's category has a continuous eligibility period that is still running when the state file reports an income above the category's limit. The member is not moved out of the category.
- A member's category has no continuous eligibility, and the state file reports a changed income in the fourth month of the eligibility period. The new income is applied at the next renewal, not in that fourth month.
- The state file prints an income of 147 percent. It is compared as 147; no figure such as 147.4 is formed or rounded by Prairie Ridge.
